Main Street AI
Our town, learning together

Practical AI for the people who keep this town running.

You will sit down with people who do work like yours, try the tools on real tasks from your own week, and leave with one working shortcut you can use the next morning.

Who is in the room

The mix is the point. A CPA, a care provider, and a youth league organizer all drown in the same paperwork, and each group will hear how the others handle it. Here is what each table will work on.

Professional services

Independent CPAs · Attorneys · Insurance brokers

  • Client follow-up: first drafts of reminder emails, document requests, and appointment confirmations
  • Long documents, short version: summaries of filings, policies, and plan documents you can check in minutes
  • Client education: plain language explainers and handouts your clients actually read

Local business owners

Shops · Restaurants · Trades · Solo operators

  • Getting found: social posts, product and menu descriptions, and replies to customer reviews
  • The inbox: faster answers to the questions customers ask every single week
  • Back office: schedules, simple spreadsheets, and turning notes into invoices and lists

Senior services

In-home care providers · Senior community centers

  • Coordination: caregiver schedules, shift notes, and family update messages
  • Programming: activity calendars, newsletters, and event flyers in a fraction of the time
  • Intake: cleaner forms and follow-up lists so no referral falls through

Family and community

Childcare centers · Libraries · Youth sports organizers

  • Parent communication: newsletters, enrollment emails, and last minute schedule changes
  • Volunteer wrangling: sign-up messages, reminders, and thank-you notes for sponsors and helpers
  • Programs: event descriptions, reading lists, and registration answers on demand

How the two hours run

Short demos, long practice. Roughly a third of the session is presentation; the rest is you, working on your own material, with help walking the room.

  1. 0:00 to 0:15

    Welcome and a plain English tour

    What today's AI tools actually do well, where they fall short, and the safety basics for client and family information. A hello from the host, then quick introductions around the room.

  2. 0:15 to 0:45

    Live demos on real local work

    Watch a week's worth of small tasks get done in minutes: a client reminder email, a senior center newsletter, a rain-out message for a youth league, a reply to a one-star review.

  3. 0:45 to 1:20

    Build-along: one workflow of your own

    Pick one recurring task from your own work and build it step by step at your table. Helpers circulate so nobody gets stuck on a login screen.

  4. 1:20 to 1:45

    Sector tables

    Break into small groups by line of work, professional services, business owners, senior services, family and community, and trade prompts, templates, and the questions specific to your field.

  5. 1:45 to 2:00

    Questions, and what happens next

    Open Q&A, a printed starter pack to take home, and how to get free one-on-one follow-up help after the workshop if you want to go further.

What you leave with

One working shortcut

A workflow you built yourself, on your own laptop, for a task you really do every week. Not a demo account, not a hypothetical.

A starter pack of prompts

Printed and digital prompts written for your line of work, ready to copy, paste, and adjust, including the safety checklist.

People to call

New contacts across town doing similar work, plus an open door for free follow-up help as you put the tools to use.

A community day, in a community place

The first session is planned for a local library or community center, and the Chamber of Commerce is being invited to partner on the day. Libraries and community centers are where this town already goes to learn, they are free to walk into, and they sit in the middle of every group this workshop is for.

Seats will be limited to keep the hands-on help real, and the room will be mixed on purpose: professionals next to business owners, care providers next to coaches.

Date, venue, and the Chamber partnership are being finalized. Register your interest below and you will be the first to get the date, the location, and a seat reservation link. Interest also helps us pick a room big enough.

Doing this responsibly

Many people in the room handle other people's sensitive information for a living. The workshop treats that as the starting point, not an afterthought.

Keep private data out

We practice on sample and scrubbed material, and cover exactly what should never be pasted into a general AI tool, client files, health details, and financial records included.

A human checks everything

AI drafts, people decide. Anything headed to a client, a family, or a filing gets read by the professional responsible for it first.

Know the limits

Tools can be confidently wrong. We cover the quick checks that catch errors before they reach a client, a parent, or a senior.
